# Were later-joining MHSDS providers disproportionately CYP services?

**Claim tier: `DESCRIPTIVE_EVIDENCE_ONLY`. Released: no.** Generated by `scripts/mhsds_cyp_cohort.py`; every figure below is in `data/mhsds_cyp_cohort.json`.

`docs/PROJECT_V2_SPECIFICATION.md` §4 item 1 names this question as the one that "directly determines whether adolescent-specific trends are artefactual". The warning box in `docs/REFERRAL_BASELINE.md` names it as "plausible and has not been checked". It has now been checked as far as the archive permits, which is not as far as the question needs.

## The verdict

**The withdrawn comparator claim should STAY WITHDRAWN, but not because the confounder was demonstrated - because it cannot be excluded from this archive. The question §4 item 1 poses is not answerable from MHSDS.**

Decided by: neither classifier reached a testable state.

Because the broad classifier's association with join date (+0.589, n=189, p=0.0000) collapses to +0.039 once provider size is controlled, and the smallest size stratum contains no continuous-cohort provider at all, so there is no common support to adjust across; the unconfounded classifier reaches only 3 joiner(s) against 53 cohort providers, below the 10 needed on each side.

What little unconfounded evidence exists points TOWARD the confounder: the 3 joiners with a measurable under-18 share have a median of 0.999 against a cohort median of 0.136. It flips on the inclusion of a single provider (see the threshold table below) and is not a result.

## What the archive cannot do, stated before what it can

The decisive analysis as the brief specifies it - the AS08 fixed-cohort computation restricted to the under-18 band, over the comparator window 2017/18-2023/24 - **cannot be computed from this archive.** Not underpowered: absent. This was established by enumerating every `Provider`-breakdown measure in the archive before any statistic was computed.

- There is no provider-by-age breakdown anywhere (`provider_by_age_breakdown_exists`: False). Age appears only as `England; Age`, which carries no provider dimension and so admits no cohort restriction.
- Every provider-level age split begins **2023-04**. The comparator window closes 2024-03.
- `England; Age` itself begins **2022-04**, so even the England-level under-18 series does not reach back into the window.

**Half the withdrawn claim is untestable in MHSDS at any cohort size, ever.** MHSDS publishes 'England; Age' and 'England; Gender' as two separate breakdowns of the same England total. No breakdown in the archive crosses age with sex at any geography, and constructing one would require summing across nesting levels. The 'emerging female excess within the adolescent band' half of the withdrawn claim has no MHSDS test at any cohort size.

## The cohort and the joiners

Over 2017-04 to 2024-03, 539 providers appear at least once; **71** publish a usable MHS01 value in every month (AS08's cohort); **309** are present in the final month but absent or unusable in the first. Providers present rose 92 to 397.

All ages, recomputed here: the cohort rises x1.411 against x1.517 unrestricted, so 82.6% of the log growth survives restriction. Joiners hold 13.9% of activity in 2024-03. **This is all ages and does not answer the age-specific question**; it is here so the reader has AS08's context on the same page.

Join month is the first month a provider published a **usable** MHS01 value. 716 providers have one, 2016-05 to 2026-06.

## Classifier 1 - CYP intensity index (broad, and refuted as a size artefact)

Definition: MHS110 (closed referrals for CYP aged 0-17 with at least two contacts) over the same provider's MHS01, over months where both are usable.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Providers | 189 |
| Distinct join months | 54 |
| Spearman rho, join month vs index | **+0.5889** |
| Permutation p (two-sided, 20000 draws) | 0.00005 |
| Minimum detectable rho at 80% power | 0.203 |
| Spearman rho, join month vs log provider size | -0.7431 |
| Spearman rho, index vs log provider size | -0.7698 |
| **Partial rho, controlling for size** | **+0.0394** |

The raw association is large and would, taken alone, say later joiners were far more CYP-focused. Controlling for provider size removes it. The index is a CYP flow over an all-ages stock and is mechanically larger for small providers; later joiners are much smaller. This classifier therefore cannot answer the question.

The partial correlation assumes the confounding is monotone in ranks. Stratifying assumes nothing of the kind, and agrees:

| Size tertile | n | Median index | rho join vs index | Cohort n | Joiners n | Cohort median | Joiners median | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | 63 | 0.1197 | +0.047 | 0 | 56 | - | - | - |
| mid | 63 | 0.0795 | +0.082 | 10 | 50 | 0.0429 | 0.0858 | 0.1171 |
| large | 63 | 0.0146 | -0.142 | 56 | 5 | 0.0150 | 0.0078 | 0.3178 |

**Common support is the deeper problem.** Of 111 joiners carrying an index, 52 fall inside the size range the two groups share; of 66 cohort providers, 38 do. The smallest size tertile contains no continuous-cohort provider at all. Over most of the joiners' size range there is nothing to compare them to, and no reweighting can manufacture a comparison where the data has none.

## Classifier 2 - under-18 share (unconfounded, and too sparse to decide)

Definition: median across measure families of (published under-18 sibling / its own published parent), per provider.

Numerator and denominator are the same published measure, from the same provider, for the same month. Nothing is summed, no nesting level is crossed, and provider size cannot enter - which is exactly what Classifier 1 lacked. No provider name is read at any point.

| Family | Measure | Providers with a share | Median share | Mean within-provider SD |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CCR70 | New emergency referrals to crisis care teams | 22 | 0.283 | 0.133 |
| CCR71 | New urgent referrals to crisis care teams | 44 | 0.119 | 0.053 |
| CCR73 | New urgent crisis referrals reaching a face-to-face contact | 33 | 0.166 | 0.067 |
| CCR117 | New very urgent referrals to crisis care teams | 17 | 0.455 | 0.113 |
| CCR118 | New very urgent crisis referrals reaching a face-to-face contact | 13 | 0.770 | 0.103 |
| CCR119 | New very urgent crisis referrals seen within 4 hours | 12 | 0.790 | 0.109 |
| CCR120 | New urgent crisis referrals seen within 24 hours | 25 | 0.158 | 0.088 |
| PLS121 | New referrals to liaison psychiatry teams from A&E | 41 | 0.082 | 0.020 |
| PLS122 | A&E liaison referrals reaching a face-to-face contact | 39 | 0.089 | 0.028 |
| PLS123 | A&E liaison referrals seen within 1 hour | 36 | 0.083 | 0.031 |

**57 providers carry a share at all: 53 from the continuous cohort and 3 joiners.** The parent measures are crisis-care and A&E-liaison referral counts, run by a minority of providers: across the observation window the parent is missing in roughly 93% of provider-months. The joiners are also small, so their cells are the ones most often suppressed - and a suppressed cell is excluded, never read as zero.

| Min months required | Providers | Cohort n | Joiners n | Cohort median | Joiner median | Joiner shares | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12 | 57 | 53 | 3 | 0.136 | 0.999 | 0.764, 0.999, 1.000 | 0.0163 |
| 6 | 59 | 55 | 3 | 0.136 | 1.000 | 0.764, 1.000, 1.000 | 0.0146 |
| 3 | 61 | 56 | 4 | 0.133 | 0.882 | 0.054, 0.764, 1.000, 1.000 | 0.1544 |

Read the last two columns together. The joiners that can be measured do look like CYP services - shares near 1.0 against a cohort median near 0.14 - and at the stricter thresholds the contrast is nominally significant. But it rests on three organisations, and admitting a fourth at the loosest threshold moves p from about 0.02 to about 0.20. **A result that turns on one provider is not a result**, and NON-NEGOTIABLE 4 says to state the size and stop rather than present it as one.

## The under-18 fixed cohort, on the only window where it can be run

**Window 2023-04 to 2026-06.** The comparator window is 2017/18-2023/24. This one opens 2023-04, inside its final year, and runs past it. Provider participation is also nearly flat here (381 to 417 against 4.32x over the comparator window), so there is no coverage ramp for a cohort restriction to remove and the test has nothing to bite on.

| Family | Continuous under-18 cohort size | Providers present first/last | Cohort ratio | Unrestricted ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CCR70 | 3 | 381/417 | x0.761 | x0.410 |
| CCR71 | 19 | 381/417 | x1.123 | x1.119 |
| CCR73 | 13 | 381/417 | x1.240 | x1.216 |

| PLS122 | 21 | 381/417 | x1.061 | x1.071 |
| PLS123 | 15 | 381/417 | x1.144 | x1.274 |

Cohort size is stated before the trend, as required. These ratios **must not** be read as the comparator test: the window sits at and beyond the comparator's end, and provider participation is nearly flat across it, so there is no coverage ramp for the restriction to remove.

## England age bands, published separately

Bands are never merged. `England; Age` publishes single years 16 and 17 beside "11 to 15"; summing them into an "under 18" is the merge this project forbids. These are England totals with no provider dimension, so no cohort restriction is possible on them - they are context, not a test.

## What `docs/REFERRAL_BASELINE.md` needs

That file is not edited by this script. What its warning box needs, on this evidence:

- The sentence "If the providers joining later were disproportionately children and young people's services - which is plausible and has not been checked" should be updated to record that it HAS now been checked against MHSDS and that MHSDS cannot answer it, citing this file. The withdrawal stands, but its status changes from "unchecked" to "unanswerable from this source".
- The box's promised remedy - "restrict to providers submitting continuously across the whole window" - should be corrected. That restriction was run (AS08) and works for ALL AGES only. It cannot be run for the under-18 band, because MHSDS publishes no provider-level age split before 2023-04 and no provider-by-age breakdown at all.
- The sex-ratio section must stay withdrawn and should be marked **untestable in MHSDS**, not merely unchecked. There is no age-by-sex cross-tab at any level, so no future provider-cohort work on this archive will change it.
- The box should record that the one candidate classifier that WAS broad enough to test - CYP closed referrals over all-ages activity - showed a large apparent effect that vanished on adjustment for provider size. A successor tempted by the same index should find that already tried and refuted here.
- Whatever is written there, Fingertips indicator 93623 is a different collection from MHSDS with its own compilation. This analysis constrains a proposed mechanism, not that indicator's numbers directly.
- What would actually settle it: a provider-by-age extract of MHSDS covering 2017/18-2023/24, which is not in the published time series and would need a data request - the same route as the FOI already drafted under `studies/foi_requests/`.

## Limits

- **Both classifiers are measured from 2023-04 and applied to joins dated from 2016.** A provider's case mix is assumed stable enough to carry backwards. The measured within-provider month-to-month spread of the share averages 0.074 across families - evidence over 39 months, not over nine years. A provider that converted from adult to CYP work after joining is misclassified.
- **The unconfounded share is measured on crisis-care and A&E-liaison referral routes**, the only provider-level age splits published. They are not the general referral flow the comparator measured, and a provider could be CYP-heavy in routine referrals without being so in crisis referrals.
- **Providers that merged, split or changed organisation code leave the continuous cohort by construction**, so the cohort is not a random sample. AS08's limit, inherited unchanged.
- **MHS01 is a stock, not the referral flow** the comparator measured. MHS32 at provider level begins 2022-04 and cannot cover the window.
- **Counts, not rates.** No population denominator is applied here; that is AS11's job.
- **The joiner set is defined by presence in the window's last month and absence in its first.** A provider that joined mid-window and left before 2024-03 is in neither group, so the two groups do not exhaust the archive.

**Compatibility is not support.** No mechanism was calibrated here, so `compare_mechanisms` was not invoked and nothing inherits its refutation asymmetry in either direction. What this file does is refute one candidate *classifier* and report that the question itself is out of reach of this archive.
